The introduction opens on the puzzling scenario (a working storefront selling sold-out jackets), not on a dictionary definition, a sweeping claim or an announcement.

p40 and p43 answer the chapter's so-what (visibility and switches, a plan written as a journey with a name in every row); p45-p47 give the part's synthesis, the answer in the joins and the walk for the reader's own landscape.

p40 returns to the opening storefront and names page availability as the wrong measure; p45 under 'Closing Part IX' returns to the part opening's warehouse and storefront and names each journey's incident.

The intro reader predicted the evening told twice (2026 incident: week, Friday with three mechanisms, weekend; 2027 plan with forecast, capacity, order path, stock events, switches, runbook, rehearsal, what goes wrong), the closing of Part IX, the fixed totals versus labelled reconstructions, and the peak-load chapter's methods from dated Shopify, Zalando and AWS practice.

The reader locates the failure behind the platform (rate-limited one-at-a-time order flow behind from about 13:00 in an unwatched queue; scheduled stock copies) and lists forecast, per-link tests with marked orders, batches keyed on the order number, a queue-age alarm, a dead-letter queue with an owner, stock events, owned and triggered switches, situation room and dashboard, vendor clause and the 08:00 reconciliation. It omits the change freeze, the 1.5x figure and the never-switched-off essentials, which the draft carries (Plan ¶2, ¶4, ¶6); the substance is present.

The reader explains the two-hour window by design, harmless when nothing sells out inside it, the 19:40/19:45/20:30/21:35 times, 1,340 units split 790/550, the marketplace cost and bol's warning, and the fix by stock events through an availability service with per-channel buffers within a minute; only the fallback is left out.

The reader gives every 2026 action in the expected answer (hand zeroing of 24 variants, connector hand edits with no pause switch, vendor ticket 21:30 / answer 22:40, mass e-mail, theme sentence, no orders-per-minute view) and the 2027 switches with owners and triggers, dashboard, incident commander, vendor contact and templates with OMS order numbers.
